Subject: Close sequencing: acceptance gates & legal handoffs for PulseCure pilot

David —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and legal at PulseCure are trying to lock down the signing sequence so we can hit our pilot start date (target week of Nov 15). Two asks from our side: a concise mutual action plan (MAP) that maps internal owners to acceptance gates (functional tests, data handling verification, SLA review) and clarity on the sequencing of MSA / DPA / order form signature (we'd prefer the DPA to be executed before the order form, if possible).

High-level constraints:
- Pilot must start by 2026-11-15 (hard)
- Security review complete by 2026-11-05
- PO needs to be issued no later than 2026-11-10

Can you send a MAP with named owners, target dates, and any evidence artifacts we should expect for each gate? Also please call out any dependencies that require legal to sign earlier than the order form. Our legal lead is copied on this thread (procurement@pulsecure.com).

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround on this.

Best,
Ava Simmons
Head of Strategic Procurement
PulseCure

Ava —

Thanks for the clear constraints. I put together an initial MAP that maps acceptance gates to owners and proposed target dates. Key callouts up front:
- We recommend executing the DPA prior to order form signature as you indicated (this avoids having any production data processing tied to an unsigned privacy agreement).
- Security evidence (SOC2 excerpt, dataflow diagram, retention policy) can be provided as a stub for review immediately; full evidence package will be uploaded to your SecureShare folder once we have an NDA in place.

Attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx — high-level lanes + owners + artifacts.

Next steps I propose:
1) PulseCure legal confirms DPA reviewer and target sign date (can you confirm a legal contact?)
2) Redwood provides security evidence stub by 2026-11-01 (we'll share the redacted SOC2 excerpt).
3) Joint acceptance checklist agreed by 2026-11-05 so engineering can schedule the pilot cutover week of 2026-11-15.

Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the MAP and dependencies — Karthik, Laura: looping you in for sequencing and acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Solutions

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 5:03 PM David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Ava —
> 
> Thanks for the clear constraints. I put together an initial MAP that maps acceptance gates to owners and proposed target dates.

Thanks David — adding the sequencing checklist below to make the dependencies explicit. I'm proposing minimal gating so we don't delay the pilot, with fallbacks if a gate slips.

Sequencing checklist (proposal):
- Pre-sign (week of 10/26–11/01): DPA draft to PulseCure legal for review (owner: PulseCure legal).
- Evidence delivery (by 11/01): Redwood delivers redacted SOC2 excerpt, architecture diagram, data handling one-pager (owner: Redwood security). [attachment: security-evidence-stub.pdf]
- Acceptance test definition (by 11/05): Joint list of 5 smoke tests + success criteria (owner: PulseCure engineering / Redwood SE).
- Order form (by 11/10): Commercials agreed; signature window open after DPA executed (owner: PulseCure procurement / Redwood finance).
- Cutover & pilot start (11/15): Sandbox -> production toggle; rollback plan agreed (owner: PulseCure ops / Redwood infra).

Fallbacks & mitigations:
- If DPA sign is delayed beyond 11/05, we can start a limited sandbox pilot (no customer PII) while legal finishes DPA; full production traffic requires DPA in place.
- If evidence delivery slips, we can provide signed attestations and schedule a secure evidence room review for 11/08–11/10.

Operational notes (short):
- Suggested SLA tier for pilot: 99.9% uptime, 50ms median gen latency target — final in order form.
- Acceptance requires 7/10 successful runs for the smoke test suite across 3 consecutive days.

I've attached the evidence stub and an updated MAP worksheet with owners filled. David / Laura: please confirm the dates align with your capacity. Ava: can you confirm who on your legal side will own the DPA review and the contact email?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
